subject: Renewal: multi-year ramp + credit schedule to secure rates
body:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harris <ben.harris@solenate.com>
Cc: Claire Moreno <claire.moreno@solenate.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: multi-year ramp + credit schedule to secure rates

Ben —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on the usage profile you shared and your desire to keep predictability in 2027+ while avoiding large step-ups, I sketched a multi-year prepay structure that (1) locks unit rates for the term, (2) phases the prepaid dollars to match expected product adoption, and (3) includes an underutilization credit so you don't lose committed value in year 1.

Highlights (high level):
- Term: 3 years (Jan 1, 2027 — Dec 31, 2029)
- Yearly prepay schedule (cash flow-friendly): Year1 = 40% of 3yr committed spend, Year2 = 30%, Year3 = 30%
- Effective discount vs list for committed usage: Year1 effective 18% off list, Year2 effective 22%, Year3 effective 25% (volume and term blended)
- Underutilization protection: Up to 20% of Year1 unused prepaid capacity can be converted to a credit applied against Year2 usage or rolled into professional services (one-time, no cash refund)
- Ramp credit: If actual consumed tokens exceed the Year1 prepaid baseline by >30% in Q4 2027, we apply a one-time invoice credit equal to 50% of the overage up to a cap of $50k (to smooth the transition)
- Price protection: Unit rates for covered SKUs are fixed for the full 3-year term.

I've attached a draft term sheet (Redwood_MultiYear_TermSheet_v3.pdf) and included a short usage extract from Q1–Q2 for context.

Next steps I propose:
1) Your procurement/legal reviews the attached term sheet and confirms any non-standard clauses.
2) If helpful, I can put Marissa (contracts) and Vivek (finance) on a quick call to walk through billing cadence and accounting implications.
3) If you want to move forward, we can issue a SOW/Order Form and DocuSign it — target timeline to preserve current list rates would be signing by Sep 3.

Would you prefer a 2- or 3-year window in the first pass? I recommended 3 to maximize price protection but can tighten to 2 if you want lower near-term commitments.

Cheers,
Connor
---
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123


On Mon, 2 Aug 2026 at 11:45 AM Ben Harris <ben.harris@solenate.com> wrote:

Connor,

Appreciate the clear write-up. A few quick notes from our side after an internal review with product and procurement:
- We like the Year1 light in cashflow approach, that helps.
- The underutilization protection is important — we take the risk of lower adoption in H1 2027.
- Procurement flagged the rollover language: they prefer credits to be automatically applied to future consumption rather than needing an opt-in to convert to services.
- Legal asked whether SLA credits or service credits would be forfeited if we move to a prepaid plan that includes price protection — they want assurance critical SLOs remain enforceable.

Could you have your team adjust the term sheet to automatically apply Year1 rollover credits to Year2 consumption by default, and include a brief SLA addendum clarifying no change to core SLO remedies?

—Ben


On Mon, 2 Aug 2026 at 15:20 Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com> wrote:

Ben — thanks, good feedback.

We can make the rollover automatic (credit applies to Year2 consumption unless you explicitly request conversion to professional services). I've asked Marissa to update the term sheet language to that effect and to add an SLA addendum paragraph to confirm existing SLO remedies remain unchanged for the covered SKUs.

Two internal items I want to flag (copying Marissa & Vivek):
- Marissa: procurement asked about a Payment Plan option (monthly installments against the annual prepay). Can Finance support a 3-month installment option in Year1 for cashflow? If yes, we can offer that without changing the overall discount.
- Vivek: we may need an exception on the standard revenue recognition notes if we allow installment billing — what's the minimum certification finance needs to approve?

I'll circulate a clean Term Sheet v4 once Marissa updates it.

Connor


On Tue, 3 Aug 2026 at 09:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:

Connor / Team / Ben,

Attached: updated term sheet (v4) with automatic Year1->Year2 rollover credit language and a short SLA addendum. Finance confirmed we can support a 3-month installment plan in Year1 (monthly invoices, net 30 per installment). Practical notes:
- Installment billing requires Solenate to provide a PO and sign the Order Form before we start installment invoices.
- For revenue recognition the finance team requires a signed Order Form and confirmation of the billing schedule; no additional revenue exceptions beyond standard policy.
- We can include an optional mid-term true-up at the end of each year to reconcile actual usage vs committed; overages billed at the contracted unit rate, with the previously mentioned ramp credit applied if Q4 usage exceeds baseline by >30%.

Ben — if that looks ok, we can update the DocuSign envelope and route to your procurement mailbox (procurement@solenate.com).

Best,
Marissa


On Thu, 5 Aug 2026 at 16:44:00 -0700 Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:

Quick internal note to Connor & Marissa before we send final to Ben:
- Finance approves the 3-month installment option for Year1. We will need the Order Form to include the installment schedule and the PO number.
- Approving the ramp credit language is ok, but revenue needs the credit defined as an offset to future invoices (not as a liability reserve) for accounting clarity.
- If the customer requests an early cash refund instead of rollover, we need legal approval; default remains credit-to-invoice.

Connor — feel free to move forward and add the PO/DocuSign links to the HubSpot deal. I marked a small commercial flexibility line: if Solenate signs and prepays at 50% of the 3yr committed spend in Year1 (instead of 40%), we can add a 2% additional discount to the blended rate (requires CRO approval).

Vivek
